items.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models

items.editor_note: Proposes learning when to commit tokens, reducing the decoding rounds dLLMs need.

items.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
items.summary_1line: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated....
items.editor_note: Extends the efficiency push to agents by adapting compute spent and text generated per interaction.

editorial.tldr: Diffusion language models first appeared here as the backbone of a tool-using chemistry agent. Days later they turned up on the offensive side, as a way to craft fluent black-box attacks on LLMs.
editorial.whats_new: A second arXiv paper in two days targets dLLM inference speed: Metacognitive Decoding adapts where compute is spent and how much text is generated, aimed at diffusion-based agents.
editorial.why_it_matters: Diffusion LLMs only pay off for serving if parallel decoding cuts rounds without hurting quality; two decoding papers in two days show the effort, but it is research-stage evidence, not a deployable runtime.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet; if you prototype one, measure decoding rounds and quality against your autoregressive baseline, and include fluent-prompt attacks in red-team evals.

status.detail: Four arXiv papers, no production release: agents, attacks and two decoding-speed approaches.

beats.headline: Masked diffusion LMs drive a tool-integrated chemistry agent
Diffusion LMs used for perplexity-aware black-box attacks
Schedule distillation aims to cut dLLM decoding rounds
Metacognitive Decoding targets efficient diffusion-based agents

open_questions: Do the schedule-distillation and metacognitive-decoding speedups hold on independent benchmarks at equal output quality?
Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
